stick_real_estate_mortgage_cap_rate_ltv_.question: Real estate - mortgage, cap rate, LTV and coverage, sealed
references: The annuity (amortization) formula M = P r (1+r)^n / ((1+r)^n - 1) - a geometric series, public domain
Appraisal Institute, The Appraisal of Real Estate, 15th ed. (2020) - income capitalization
Fannie Mae Selling Guide B2-1.2: the 80 percent LTV line for mortgage insurance
stick_real_estate_mortgage_cap_rate_ltv_.statement: Property finance is the annuity formula and five ratios: payment, NOI over value, price over rent, loan over value, NOI over debt service, rent over value.

ticks.claim: [a 30-year mortgage, SEALED] $300,000 at 6.5 percent over 360 months: M = P r (1+r)^n / ((1+r)^n - 1) with r = 0.065/12 gives $1,896.20 a month (sealed through real_estate.RE_VERIFY). The annuity formula is the sum of a geometric series: the loan equals the present value of the payments.

[the same loan over 15 years, SEALED] 180 months: $2,613.32 (sealed through real_estate.RE_VERIFY) - 38 percent more a month, but $392,000 less interest over the life of the loan (6.5 percent: $382,633 interest at 30 years against $170,398 at 15). Time is the lender's price.
[cap rate, SEALED] NOI $24,000 on a $400,000 property is 6.0 percent (sealed through real_estate.RE_VERIFY): the unlevered yield the income capitalization approach prices on.
[gross rent multiplier, SEALED] $300,000 over $24,000 of annual rent is 12.5 (sealed through real_estate.RE_VERIFY): years of gross rent in the price, before expenses.
[loan-to-value, SEALED] $240,000 on $300,000 appraised is 80 percent (sealed through real_estate.RE_VERIFY): the line at which conventional lenders stop requiring mortgage insurance.

[debt-service coverage, SEALED] NOI $24,000 over $22,755 of annual debt service is 1.055 (sealed through real_estate.RE_VERIFY): the income covers the payments with 5.5 percent to spare - below the 1.25 most lenders want.
[gross rental yield, SEALED] $18,000 of rent on a $400,000 property is 4.5 percent (sealed through real_estate.RE_VERIFY).

[the conventions, CITED] 80 percent LTV (Fannie Mae), a 1.25 DSCR floor, a 'good' cap rate - these are lender and market conventions, chosen and changeable, cited never sealed. The annuity formula is a theorem; the ratios are definitions; what a property is WORTH is a forecast and is declined. Nothing here is investment advice.
ticks.source: Fannie Mae Selling Guide B2-1.2; Appraisal Institute (2020); src/concordance/verifiers/real_estate.py

ticks.claim: [on the one map] Property finance is the economics floor's time value of money (card_floor_economics; the economics stick: present value, compound interest) with the compounding of e (the e stick: (1 + r/n)^n) applied to one asset class. The same annuity formula prices a bond, a pension and a car loan.
